findings.reason: a builder following the named function either keys on the wrong process or never takes the host branch in production, leaving the duplication this section exists to stop while the done-when passes.
findings.text: the deliverable tells the builder to key the claim on "the host's owner (the Claude process and its start tick, as `_session_host_owner` names it)", but `SessionHost._spawn` stamps a child with `RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER = (os.getpid(), host start)` (`reckon/crew/session_host.py:435-437`), so the follower's own reader `follower_owner()` (`reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:501`) yields the host process, not the Claude process `_session_host_owner()` returns (`reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:500`, from `CLAUDE_PID`); and `_session_host_owner()` returns a value for any follower under Claude Code, so it cannot separate "a follower a session host runs" from "a follower with no host" — the very branch the deliverable requires — while the marker that can (`RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER` present only when a host armed the follower) is named nowhere

findings.reason: the only stated guarantee against the transient duplication is unmeasured, so a builder can land a change that re-introduces the exact defect for the length of a reload without the gate noticing.
findings.text: the done-when states the change "must be safe while old and new followers share a pane", but neither of its two cases nor its negative control exercises an old (session-keyed) follower overlapping a new (host-keyed) one, and by construction the two key into different directories, so during a reload the same grant is claimed twice and drawn twice
